text:
On a hectic opening we read your message, and the training lead looked into it. You said your animal's booking was handled badly, the handoff felt disorganized, and the care notes you expected were not followed through with the attention you were promised. That is a fair complaint, and I want to address it directly.

At Aurelia Skyways, the Companion Animal Travel Desk treats each trip as a shared responsibility, not a passing task. When a carrier moves through the network, the ground team is supposed to keep the handoff clean, keep the paperwork aligned, and make sure the next station knows exactly what to expect. In your case, the chain did not hold as neatly as it should have, and that is on us. The training lead has reviewed the desk log, the service notes, and the transfer steps used by the ground team. We found a gap in the follow-through between services, and that gap likely created the confusion you ran into.

Here is what we are doing now. We have reinforced the transfer checklist for companion animals, reminded the ramp and acceptance teams to confirm the care notes before movement, and asked the duty planners to flag any special handling early so it is not left to chance. We are also tightening the handoff between the booking desk and the ground team so a carrier is not moved without a clear, current plan. That is routine desk work, but it matters, and we are treating it with the seriousness it deserves.

We know a pet journey is not just freight handling. It is a family matter, and it should feel steady from the first check-in to the last release. If your animal had any distress tied to our lapse, we regret that, and we are sorry for the stress it caused you.

Please keep using the Companion Animal Travel Desk for any future travel needs, and if you choose to book with Aurelia Skyways again, we will make sure the notes are reviewed with extra care before the trip begins.

Companion Animal Travel Desk
